two `*++ui_text_ptr` in one expression are unsequenced in C: read x then y explicitly (the order of the \003 code, the order SDCC evaluates); the Game Boy's 16-bit pointer arithmetic wraps, so the offset is a signed 16-bit value on the 32-bit TLCS-900 pointer

C89: declarations before statements (cc900 refuses late declarations); `dx + dy * 32u` is unsigned: on the Game Boy's 16-bit pointers it wraps to a step back, on the 32-bit TLCS-900 pointer it would jump forward: a signed 16-bit offset

K2GE scroll map: one 16-bit cell per tile (tile number and palette), so the map pointers are word pointers into SCR1 (0x9000) instead of byte pointers into the Game Boy window map; the Game Boy compares map addresses (window map 0x9C00 is 32-aligned, so `& 0xFFE0` is the start of a map row): the same test on cell indexes from the window map
a K2GE map cell holds the tile and its palette together: one scroll_rect moves both (the CGB scrolls the attribute bank in a second pass)
